newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S TRADE GAP SEEN AT $12.6 BLN IN '97-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S TRADE GAP SEEN AT $12.6 BLN IN '97-REPORT.

text.p: Poland's trade deficit is likely to grow to $12.6 billion in 1997 from last year's $8.2 billion, but the trend could then start weakening, the president of the Polish government Centre for Strategic Studies (CSS) said.

Zbigniew Kuzmiuk said on Wednesday falling cross-border trade inflows no longer kept the current account gap at low levels, but the improving business climate in European Union countries should help Polish exports.

"The level of exports will look a bit different this year, ...also because of an improving climate abroad. We expect exports growth will be higher in 1997 than in 1996 and that the negative trend (of a growing trade deficit) will not deepen," he told a news conference.
Kuzmiuk said the CSS expected Poland's exports to rise to $27.1 billion this year from $24.4 billion in 1995.
But he said imports were expected to rise to $39.7 billion from $32.6 billion last year, because of high investment demand from companies and also high household demand for consumer goods.
